name: v0.2.0
body:
🌊 If you enjoy Waves, a star on this repo goes a long way, and if you'd like to help me afford to keep developing it, consider donating.

**Waves v0.2 is here, and with it come a lot of changes I have been quietly working on since v0.1 launched a few months ago. This is by far the largest update to Waves, which is why I am bumping the version number. As always, I did my best to test everything before release, but I still expect there to be bugs. The best way you can help me is by reporting them in the [issues](https://github.com/iamprivacy/Waves/issues) with as much detail as possible.** **Financially, I'm struggling right now, and Waves has taken up all of my free time outside of working hours. If you enjoy using Waves, please make a donation (recurring donations help the most) using the Buy Me a Coffee button on the project page or the one at the foot of the app's Settings sidebar.** **Thank you for all the love and support! I hope you enjoy using Waves v0.2 as much as I enjoyed developing it!** ### ✨ Added - 🔔 A new Releases tab lists new albums, EPs and singles from the artists you follow, grouped by date (Today, This week, This month, then each earlier month), with upcoming releases under their own filter. Releases another artist leads can be hidden (Featured releases, Settings, Releases), and then never download automatically. - 🎨 Artists, on the Releases tab, shows the artists you follow three ways: Roster (cards), Shelves (each artist's releases in a row) or Ledger (a timeline of each one's releases), and Excluded lists the library artists left out so you can follow them. - ➕ Follow an artist from their page or from the Releases tab. Your TIDAL favorites are followed automatically, and Waves changes your TIDAL favorites only if you ask it to. - 📚 Import library follows the artists in your music library in one go, after you review the list; artists who share a name are matched by the albums and songs you have. - 🔢 Follow artists with at least (Settings, Library, 5 tracks by default) keeps the import from following artists you only have a song or two by. - 🔁 Follow your artists (Settings, Library, on by default) follows your library's artists as the scan finds them, when the match is exact. - ⬇️ New releases from the artists you follow can download automatically on release day (off by default), and you pick which kinds: albums, EPs, singles or guest tracks (the songs they appear on in other artists' releases). - 🔔 A desktop notification announces new releases from the artists you follow as Waves finds them (Notify me about new releases, Settings, Notifications). - 📣 A new Notifications section in Settings, off until you flip its master switch: turning it on sends a test notification (so your system can ask for permission right away), and you pick what Waves announces: finished downloads (one notification when the queue finishes by default, or one per download, or never), failed downloads, new releases, and new Waves versions found by the update check. - ⚡ New releases show up sooner: Waves checks first the artists named in TIDAL's new-releases feed and ListenBrainz's public list (Spot new releases faster, Settings, Releases). - 🧭 Also check MusicBrainz (Settings, Releases, off by default) marks releases TIDAL does not carry on the Artists timeline. - 🏷️ Genre from MusicBrainz (Settings, Tags & Artwork, off by default) writes every genre MusicBrainz lists for the release into the files a download creates, joined by the Genre separator setting ("; " by default); for a release with none or not listed yet, Artist genres for unlisted releases (on by default) uses the artist's, taken from Look up your artists on MusicBrainz when it already knows the artist. Files already in your library are never retagged. - 🧭 Look up your artists on MusicBrainz (Settings, Library, off by default) keeps your library artists' genres and albums and helps tell same-name artists apart. - 🔎 Every Releases page has a search box (Cmd+F, or Ctrl+F on Windows and Linux). - 🎬 Music videos from the artists you follow show on the Releases tab (Music videos setting to hide them), and CHECK NOW checks every artist again at once. - 🏷️ Covers on the Releases tab, on Browse and at the top of an album carry two small corner dots: one says the album is in your library, the other its quality (the best it offers up to your audio quality setting, or ATMOS); pointing at the cover opens them into words. - 📄 The download queue can export the tracks that did not download as a CSV (REPORT on a row, MISSING REPORT for everything), and an open row can list only its missing tracks ([issue #54](https://github.com/iamprivacy/Waves/issues/54)). - 📏 How many tracks an open queue row shows before it scrolls is a setting (Appearance, 12 by default). - ☕ A Buy Me a Coffee button sits at the foot of the Settings sidebar, above the credit. - ⬇️ The QUEUE button in the header now shows how your downloads are going: it becomes a little speed chart with the percent done and the download speed, the count rolls as items arrive and finish, and the count flashes red and shakes when one fails. - ✨ When a download lands, the QUEUE button's count bumps and throws off a ring of sparks; when the last one lands, the count shatters into pieces that fall back together as a check. - 💧 While a download finishes its last steps, the chart in the QUEUE button settles into one level and fills to the brim as each step lands, then shows DONE. ### 🔧 Changed - 📅 Release dates show month, day and year in full (09-04-2026) everywhere. - 📚 A first library scan reads one album from every artist before the rest, so Import library finds your artists much sooner. - 🏷️ The library index now keeps each file's tags, so the first scan after updating reads every file once more in the background. - 🧭 Settings is a sidebar of sections in three groups (Music, Files, App) with one section shown at a time, and it reopens on the section you last used; Up and Down step through the sections once the sidebar is clicked. - 🧩 The Advanced section is gone and its settings moved: motion and hover effects to Appearance, download speed and pauses to Speed & Pacing (joined by Concurrent track downloads and the download delay from Downloads), tag options to Tags & Artwork, downsampling and the FLAC signatures check to FFmpeg & FLAC, and the two resets to the end of Diagnostics. - 🎛️ Every choice shows its options side by side instead of in a drop-down, the download delay and the pause between batches each sit on one row, and switches sit in even rows with shorter names (Clean Album Artist is now "Primary album artist in tags", under Tags & Artwork). - 🏷️ Three sections have new names: File organization is now Files & Naming, Metadata & artwork is now Tags & Artwork, and Processing (FFmpeg) is now FFmpeg & FLAC. "Show every edition on artist pages" is now "All editions on artist pages", beside "Most-complete edition only" in Discography & Editions, and in Library "Bulk downloads skip what you have" is now "Skip what you already have" and "Confirm uncertain matches with MusicBrainz" is now "Ask MusicBrainz when unsure". - 📜 Every page has a new scrollbar, and dragging it on the Releases feed shows the month you are at. - 🖼️ A cover that is still loading shows a grid of dots, and one that could not load shows a red x. - 📦 Waves now uses newer versions of requests (2.34.2), urllib3 (2.8.0), mutagen (1.48.1) and certifi (2026.7.22). - 🔔 The new releases count on the Releases tab now glows in and counts up as releases arrive, then counts back down and shrinks away when you open Releases, instead of popping in and out. ### 🐛 Fixed - 📶 A track whose connection dropped partway through is fetched again before it counts as failed, and a track that does fail no longer shows FINISHING first. - 🐧 On Linux, the controls on a Browse card fit again: DOWNLOADED no longer touches the edge of the cover, and a console card shows PREVIEW instead of just its icon. - 🖐️ A fast trackpad swipe no longer throws a page back to where it began on macOS. - 📜 An open queue row now scrolls through every track of a long playlist instead of hiding the rest past 500 tracks, with a slim scrollbar beside the rows ([issue #54](https://github.com/iamprivacy/Waves/issues/54)). - 🎬 Waves finds an FFmpeg installed with Homebrew, MacPorts or Linuxbrew when opened from the Finder, the Dock or a desktop launcher, and passes over a broken one left behind instead of downloading with it or showing it as installed. - 🧭 Ask MusicBrainz when unsure (Settings, Library) now reaches MusicBrainz on a Mac without Homebrew's OpenSSL; before, every request failed quietly there. - 🔗 A TIDAL share link that ends in /u, a slash or a query opens again instead of reading "Could not open that link". - 💾 After macOS ejects a network share, Waves mounts it back by itself again when the share's name has a space or when the folder you use was mounted from inside a share. - 🛑 A mix queued after you stopped another download no longer fails straight away. - 📁 A playlist, mix, album or song whose name holds a template token such as {artist_name} now stays in one folder instead of being split per artist. - 📂 A download folder typed with .. in it now saves into that folder, and a file briefly locked on Windows after conversion no longer fails the track. - 🎤 When LRCLIB has only plain lyrics for a song, Waves now uses TIDAL's timed lyrics if it has them, so you get a .lrc file instead of a .txt. - ⚙️ A switch set to "false" by editing the settings file by hand now loads as off instead of turning itself back on. - 🗂️ A bulk download no longer replaces files you already have: a copy Waves finds in the folder is checked for its quality, and one that does need an upgrade keeps the tags you added (Genre, Comment, Mood and the like) ([issue #55](https://github.com/iamprivacy/Waves/issues/55)). - 🏷️ If the ownership file in the Waves settings folder is removed or replaced while the app is open, Browse cards still show which albums and playlists you already have. - 📏 A downloading row's progress bar in the queue now resizes while you drag the queue edge instead of after you let go. ### 🔐 Verify | Asset | SHA-256 | | --- | --- | | `waves_linux-arm64.AppImage` | `bf26048ff9d0e7b4c468c6a7e182ca3ba4ec4eb09547429988bd4d20338e3719` | | `waves_linux-arm64.zip` | `ec778e770526fbbd65abfdf1cc1776d9299d6c7adbd47df93e14bab333262bf5` | | `waves_linux-x64.AppImage` | `cd04ffe2794cc1f421f38788315344315582dd7ffc4b8ff1a6eaea89a1d89c15` | | `waves_linux-x64.zip` | `7826b19411fb3fd7ea77ff38f6c86c2e8029a5ebcb8e7f6091605e998300e713` | | `waves_macos-apple-silicon.zip` | `d82ec16349157854faa101d76bb6f7f2fde79115a2dad6b1adadfb1735d773fe` | | `waves_macos-apple-silicon_legacy.zip` | `1b47ceb474dcecd8643f386edbe108812548e7411b9fa2b6ab8521144025866f` | | `waves_macos-intel.zip` | `95fd71be9fe5497441c381315533d678c16fc28a1695b0026b04564222d6a659` | | `waves_macos-intel_legacy.zip` | `b73803f42ef4273f8df43c109c25adb6b170e2e6d5828d5d9029f410327e28d8` | | `waves_windows-arm64.zip` | `b7a3dec5c5a15083cfb66bd2fe8bc8572dfddbbe43faae41d414926c2138fe30` | | `waves_windows-x64.zip` | `a72fe1fc1655251e36182a05c9500249af40e7432db59658651a612a8936e591` | `SHA256SUMS` lists these hashes and `SHA256SUMS.sig` is an Ed25519 signature over it, made with the Waves release key. name: v0.1.35
body:
🌊 If you enjoy Waves, a star on this repo goes a long way, and if you'd like to help me afford to keep developing it, consider donating.

### ✨ Added - 🎼 Advanced settings has a FLAC signatures check: Scan reads every FLAC header in your Waves library or in a custom location chosen with Browse (switch on Deep check to also decode the audio and find damage) and saves a CSV report of all files (View reports opens them at any time), and Fix writes the missing audio signature into the files that have none (34 header bytes each, after decoding and checking the audio), so they pass `flac -t` and strict players again. The audio is never changed, and a file that already carries a signature is never rewritten. Scans read several files at once, which makes them much faster on a network share, and a later scan reads only the files that changed since an earlier one (switch on Recheck all to read every file again). Long runs show a progress bar with the time left, and a fix that stops part way (the app closed or crashed) resumes where it left off. After updating, a one-time notice on Browse explains which files are affected and opens the check. - 🐧 The Linux AppImage now carries AppStream metadata, so software centers and the AppImage catalog show real screenshots and a description of the signed-in app instead of the first-run sign-in screen. ### 🔧 Changed - 🪟 Pop-up buttons are sized to their labels like every other button in the app, instead of stretching across the dialog. ### 🐛 Fixed - 🎼 Every extracted FLAC file is now checked against its audio MD5 signature after download; a file that arrived without one gets it computed and written, so `flac -t` and strict players (Music Assistant and others) no longer report it as corrupt. - 🎚️ Downsampling works again with the FFmpeg builds Waves installs: they have no soxr resampler, and every downsample failed the track with "Error reinitializing filters"; FFmpeg's built-in resampler now takes over when soxr is missing. - ⏭️ With Skip existing turned off, every track downloads again, including songs Waves already downloaded into another folder, so a playlist saved to a new folder gets all of its songs ([issue #53](https://github.com/iamprivacy/Waves/issues/53)). ### 🔐 Verify | Asset | SHA-256 | | --- | --- | | `waves_linux-arm64.AppImage` | `eb1ad175ad1fecddc633006060da6457a3bd35f5ba26d6f758f78b2fed374daa` | | `waves_linux-arm64.zip` | `bdef58de36950a677ac6b9162dad2dec03eab07c5e16f072f9d717096cf86525` | | `waves_linux-x64.AppImage` | `b120d733d85ae252c8350169900b2f3d6550c3c40f19b85486e373fbfb5a7c22` | | `waves_linux-x64.zip` | `52512143ca6fe4ba807720c5f5692b445d5418db6d067775b3a4d9b306df794f` | | `waves_macos-apple-silicon.zip` | `d072a8b3da17fcbc847af512e6b0ee1cf4e3b37787c4d12063be766aac6fc0c1` | | `waves_macos-apple-silicon_legacy.zip` | `99ef786e17eaac0e2455ed68a1e8fded3d8bb9821ec592856d50faf62a020479` | | `waves_macos-intel.zip` | `32e9d2d19bb5b5dc520a4e6dcc4b44d301477be3c26b261f7ac5ba5bd51909ee` | | `waves_macos-intel_legacy.zip` | `1f1b5614cb49d58d1361baf95b24725508e791cc71d0a487dafdc40e3780d952` | | `waves_windows-arm64.zip` | `94525ef145473f9b53483fea9be48ef0adebbf3c6f13474473159e1385f4490b` | | `waves_windows-x64.zip` | `47760da275e6aff7b613e97daa70c694cdea1c129bea29826e9c4c1cbedb7c4b` | `SHA256SUMS` lists these hashes and `SHA256SUMS.sig` is an Ed25519 signature over it, made with the Waves release key. body:
🌊 If you enjoy Waves, a star on this repo goes a long way, and if you'd like to help me afford to keep developing it, consider donating.

### ✨ Added - 🎧 A release that TIDAL offers in both Dolby Atmos and stereo now lists ATMOS in its quality menu beside the stereo qualities, so you can pick either one per album or song. With Download Dolby Atmos on, its badge shows ATMOS. ### 🔧 Changed - 🔊 The Write ReplayGain tags setting now explains that players which honour the tags play loud tracks quieter ([issue #48](https://github.com/iamprivacy/Waves/issues/48)). - ⚡ Artist pages and Search results appear complete as soon as they open, with no fade-in pause. - 🎤 An artist you open for the first time loads faster. - 🖱️ Resting the pointer on an artist's name prepares that artist's page, as resting on an artist card already did. ### 🐛 Fixed - 💤 Using Waves after the computer slept no longer crashes the app on macOS ([issue #47](https://github.com/iamprivacy/Waves/issues/47)). - 🔊 A song or album you download in Dolby Atmos now reads ATMOS in the download queue from the moment it is queued, and the quality menu no longer marks it as Low, AAC 96 ([issue #45](https://github.com/iamprivacy/Waves/issues/45)). - 🎚️ An album, playlist or mix button now judges your copies by the quality chosen on that album, playlist or mix, the same way its download does, so it no longer offers a download that fetches nothing or reads DOWNLOADED when the download would fetch everything again. - 🎧 Turning Download Dolby Atmos on or off now updates the download buttons right away, not only the quality badges. - 🧾 Clicking a stereo-only album again after toggling Download Dolby Atmos no longer adds a second identical row to the queue. - 🐢 Scrolling no longer stutters while a page is still filling in, on high refresh-rate displays too. - 📜 Browse listings keep loading as you scroll, and no longer show the same cards twice or freeze the window when more rows arrive. - 🧭 Opening or going Back to a Browse page no longer freezes or blanks the window while it builds. - 🎤 Long artist pages open without freezing and fill in from the top down. - 🔎 Search results no longer shift as artist cards fill in, and changing the sort no longer makes the page jump. - ### ✨ Added - 🔐 The release page now prints every download's expected SHA-256 next to it, together with the release public key and copyable verification steps; the README has a Verify a download section with the same steps for macOS, Linux and Windows. ### 🐛 Fixed - 📋 My Tidal > Playlists lists each playlist once, and playlists that were missing from the list are back ([issue #46](https://github.com/iamprivacy/Waves/issues/46)). - 🐧 The x64 Linux zip and AppImage start on Ubuntu 22.04, Debian 12 and other distributions older than Ubuntu 24.04, where they quit at launch with a GLIBC error. ### 🔐 Verify | Asset | SHA-256 | | --- | --- | | `waves_linux-arm64.AppImage` | `6d7578eada657849f7c5048d38e9c1ee35909f4224436443c9a1d4b5bb68e327` | | `waves_linux-arm64.zip` | `0c51dd01783c94c3cede907e0c6f6baa50c3e94b01de14e04a870940fab5141c` | | `waves_linux-x64.AppImage` | `17ee32502c40e87b95d6294ba430a1ee8073d658ee3bd938e12c61c8ac2e8db6` | | `waves_linux-x64.zip` | `3ef25f47946bb31648a6da6332ad5cd9ab5e54ac0b0d3d22837da2e26f8987d0` | | `waves_macos-apple-silicon.zip` | `3bed9f8e3858dbac223767d8d78561d2783d0c35a40caab5651f5bb784945f5d` | | `waves_macos-apple-silicon_legacy.zip` | `f9d56ca2991dd4087d52bc698d56b2c24fb01fbba8589034992acf591dd3c22e` | | `waves_macos-intel.zip` | `e9e15bf6a4170efd93e5f0c29017694215687c960914bb7ded4daae274cc1a59` | | `waves_macos-intel_legacy.zip` | `274f4b7ebecc2cd60f5fd3c42e30df30815b867c82a57c377ce02c876494519e` | | `waves_windows-arm64.zip` | `616bff6fe01a0858685f2c048ca91588df6758284249ec27b20edeef25feb80b` | | `waves_windows-x64.zip` | `aa552a3867f1c4ec50cb7ca5a155791317f17438cee3b86c4340d0fb921df48b` | `SHA256SUMS` lists these hashes and `SHA256SUMS.sig` is an Ed25519 signature over it, made with the Waves release key. The public key, also compiled into every build: ``` -----BEGIN PUBLIC KEY----- MCowBQYDK2VwAyEAcetggrhiqyMN5HsBCi/f2gJL75FVPOYGU/sd4dI5b+0= -----END PUBLIC KEY----- ``` From a folder holding the zip, `SHA256SUMS` and `SHA256SUMS.sig` (Linux, or macOS with OpenSSL 3 from Homebrew in place of the built-in `openssl`): ```bash printf '%s\n' '-----BEGIN PUBLIC KEY-----' 'MCowBQYDK2VwAyEAcetggrhiqyMN5HsBCi/f2gJL75FVPOYGU/sd4dI5b+0=' '-----END PUBLIC KEY-----' > waves-release.pem base64 --decode < SHA256SUMS.sig > SHA256SUMS.sig.bin openssl pkeyutl -verify -pubin -inkey waves-release.pem -rawin -in SHA256SUMS -sigfile SHA256SUMS.sig.bin grep -v '^#' SHA256SUMS | tr -d '\r' | shasum -a 256 --ignore-missing -c - ``` Windows steps and details: [Verify a download](https://github.com/iamprivacy/Waves#verify-a-download).

name: v0.1.31
body:
🌊 If you enjoy Waves, a star on this repo goes a long way, and if you'd like to help me afford to keep developing it, consider donating.

### ✨ Added - ⬇️ My Tidal > Tracks has a DOWNLOAD ALL button that queues every favorite track after confirming the count ([issue #43](https://github.com/iamprivacy/Waves/issues/43)). - ⬇️ My Tidal > Albums, Artists, Playlists, Mixes and Videos now have the same DOWNLOAD ALL button, each after confirming the count: Albums queues every favorite album, Artists every favorite artist's full discography, Playlists every playlist (folders included), Mixes every mix and Videos every favorite video. ### 🔧 Changed - 📚 My Tidal pages open faster: a page arrives knowing which rows are already in your library. - 📀 Expanding an album or playlist is faster too: its song rows arrive knowing which ones you already have. - 🔄 A My Tidal page that quietly refreshes keeps the rows it already shows, instead of rebuilding every one; an open album stays open and a selection stays selected. - ⏱️ A My Tidal page left open for a long time now quietly picks up favorites you added elsewhere, the way Browse already did. - 🗑️ A page left open for a while now notices when you delete a downloaded file outside Waves, instead of showing DOWNLOADED until you navigate. - 🎤 A playlist, mix, album or artist page left open for a long time now quietly picks up changes, such as a new release or a rebuilt editorial playlist. - 🔖 M4A files now store the ISRC where tag editors and library managers look for it, and FLAC and MP3 files carry the explicit flag the way M4A files already did. - 📝 The download delay setting now says plainly that it paces a long run. - ⏸️ On macOS, with the window hidden or minimized and nothing downloading, Waves checks a network download folder every ten minutes instead of every minute. ### 🐛 Fixed - 🔎 Pressing Enter while a pasted search is still animating in now searches the pasted text, not the animation ([issue #41](https://github.com/iamprivacy/Waves/issues/41)). - 🔙 Going back to a library artist page that failed to load no longer stops the Back and Forward history from recording later pages. - ⚙️ A settings section you once opened or closed by hand now still opens when an update notice or folder warning links to it. - 🖱️ The quality menu rows and the Browse tiles no longer bounce past their resting size when hovered. - 📂 The missing-folder, folder-unreachable and FFmpeg-missing prompts now appear above the download queue when it is open. - 🔄 An update check that could not reach the server now says "Could not check" instead of "Up to date", for both Waves and FFmpeg. - 🔁 After signing out, the next account's Browse shelves load more again and its My Tidal sort choices start fresh. - 📥 An album or playlist downloaded earlier in the same session now opens the REDOWNLOAD prompt without a restart. - 💿 An expanded album whose track list is still loading no longer flashes DOWNLOAD over a copy you already have. - 🔙 Going back to the My Tidal category you were already on now refreshes it quietly, like every other visit. - 🧰 Turning the diagnostics toggles on or off no longer marks Settings as having unsaved changes. - 🃏 In the Console Browse layout, cards now show DONE for albums, playlists and mixes downloaded in an earlier session, and clicking one opens the redownload prompt. - 🎞️ Track rows in an expanded album no longer flash the download arrow before Waves has checked what you already downloaded. - 🔗 With "symlink to track" on, a playlist folder file that belongs to a different track is now left alone instead of being replaced by a link or moved. - 🎛️ Downloading a mix while hovering over another mix card no longer risks queuing the wrong mix's tracks. - 🃏 A Browse card built a moment after the page loaded no longer shows DOWNLOAD over an album you already downloaded. - 🔁 A RETRY that waited for FFmpeg now keeps the quality its row was queued at, even if the setting changed meanwhile. - 🎚️ Saving a new audio quality while a download is fetching a track no longer changes that track's quality. - 🏷️ A library match confirmed through MusicBrainz now shows the same badge on every card of a page, not only the ones already on screen. - 🔒 Log lines and diagnostics exports no longer include a network share's folder name, a scanner failure's file path, or a stream address. - 🙈 The "also hide titles and searches" export switch now hides a title that contains « or » and very long titles in full. - 🫧 A paused preview's cover no longer keeps animating on hidden tabs or in a minimized window. - 🖼️ A release shown in two places in Browse keeps updating its download status after one of the two cards goes away. - 🎬 A hover video that fails while its full-quality version is ready now keeps playing instead of pausing. - 📋 The download queue opens faster when Completed is collapsed with many finished items. - 🔍 Switching the search result filter to Albums or Tracks is quicker. - 🎬 Picking a video quality in the player no longer stalls playback for a moment. - 🧭 A Browse page is no longer shown before it has finished building. - 🚀 The update notice and the FFmpeg setup card now fade in with the interface instead of appearing over the launch animation. - 🧱 The tools the packaged app is built with were updated, to address a rare crash shortly after launch. - 🏷️ IN LIBRARY badges no longer fade in all over again every time you move between My Tidal categories or tabs. - 🏷️ Opening a My Tidal category while the library is still being read no longer draws the page bare and then lights every IN LIBRARY badge a moment later. - 🔗 Turning "symlink to track" off no longer makes albums downloaded while it was on read as not downloaded when your download or library folder is reached through a link. - 🎚️ A Best of Both download for an album given its own quality choice is now planned at that choice, not at the Settings quality, and the choice follows the download when it is queued under another edition. - 🔐 Signing out while My Tidal is still reading your playlists or favourites no longer lets the next account see the previous account's playlists, folders or favourites. - 🔁 RETRY after switching accounts now fetches the item again under the account that is signed in, instead of downloading through the previous one. - 📂 The Videos fold and the SHOW ALL state of every artist-page section are remembered across launches like the other sections. - 🧹 Reset application also removes the saved recent searches. - ⚙️ A settings file with an empty value or a quality this version does not know now resets just that one setting, instead of setting the whole file aside or stopping Waves from starting. - 🪟 An album or playlist whose tracks could not be loaded now says so in the panel and tries again when you collapse and expand it, instead of showing an empty list. - 🛑 Pressing STOP while a download is still waiting for its playlist folders or its details now cancels it, instead of starting it after the press. - 🚫 A download that could not fetch its item because of a rate limit or a connection drop now says "try again" instead of claiming the item is gone. - 🏠 A first Home load or a scroll that fails now says so instead of reading as an empty library, and RETRY ALL says how many rows it could not restart. - 🔎 A library rescan that fails now says so in Settings instead of returning to "Rescan" silently. - ⏳ A throttled cover-art or track server can no longer hold a download for hours: it is retried after a short wait, and STOP works. - 🔗 With "symlink to track" on, a system or share that refuses links now keeps a real copy in the playlist folder instead of leaving it empty with an empty playlist file. - 🪟 On Windows, a deep folder with non-Latin characters no longer shrinks the temporary file name so far that two tracks could share it. - 🍎 On macOS, tracks in a library or download folder whose name carries an accent are recognized as yours whichever way the volume spells the name. - 🏷️ A downloaded file that cannot be tagged is no longer filed in your library untagged and counted as done; the row fails so you can retry it. - 🔒 On macOS and Linux, the folder holding your settings, sign-in, caches and logs is now open to your account only, as the Privacy section always said. - 🖼️ A track whose separate cover.jpg fetch fails now still lands, without the cover file, instead of failing the whole track. - 🎤 Lyrics are written into the audio file only when "Embed lyrics" is on; "Save lyrics next to the track" alone now writes just the sidecar. - 🧯 A settings or sign-in file that cannot be opened no longer stops Waves from launching, and a damaged one is now kept as a backup (without replacing an older backup) before defaults are used. - 🌐 With "symlink to track" on, a library or download folder on a share that stopped answering no longer makes every ownership check wait on it at the same time. - 🗑️ On Windows, albums sitting in the NTFS recycle bin inside your library folder no longer count as owned. - 🐧 On Linux desktops without a system file picker, Browse in Settings opens a folder picker again. - 🕵️ A Windows profile name with a space in it is now fully hidden in diagnostics, not just its first word. - 🌙 A minimized Waves no longer checks TIDAL for fresher pages every five minutes. - 📜 An album playlist no longer lists the same song twice when the folder holds a stereo copy beside its Atmos copy, or an old file beside its upgrade. - 🎚️ A track borrowed from another edition in a best of both download no longer carries that edition's album loudness value. - 🏷️ A file that arrives with an empty tag block is tagged instead of failing, and a track with no album artist no longer gets an empty artist field written. - 💿 A track whose disc count is unknown is no longer tagged as disc 2 of 1. - 🎬 A finished music video that the tagger cannot open is kept instead of being reported as failed. - 🌐 A network share's server and share name no longer appear in the diagnostics log on Windows (UNC paths) or Linux (gvfs mounts). - 🔞 When an album's files or folder name say whether it is clean or explicit, the library check and the IN LIBRARY badge no longer count a clean copy as the explicit release, or the reverse, so the other edition is still downloaded. - 💿 A two-disc album kept in CD1 and CD2 folders, or kept flat and tagged per disc, now reads as complete instead of partial (such as "20 of 40"). - 🎭 A compilation with no album-artist tag can no longer stand in for an artist's album of the same name. - 📀 One disc of a multi-disc set no longer reads as the whole album when TIDAL gives no track count, and disc folders from two different editions are no longer added up into one album. - 📂 On macOS, revealing an album folder now selects it in Finder instead of opening it, so a folder named like an app is never launched. - 🎛️ A best of both download whose borrowed tracks TIDAL refuses now fetches the album's own copies instead of finishing short and blaming TIDAL. - 🎵 A radio edit that shares a code with the album version can no longer land under the album version's title, or be silently skipped, in a best of both download. - 📋 Expanding a queued album that TIDAL listed short now shows every track, including the ones that failed, and a borrowed track predicts the tier it will really land at. - 🔞 "Most-complete edition only" no longer swaps a clean album for a fuller explicit one, or the reverse, in a discography or on the artist page. - 🎤 Two different guest tracks with the same title are no longer merged into one in a discography download. - 🔊 An album offered only in Dolby Atmos that you download from now on no longer reads DOWNLOAD afterwards when Atmos is off and the quality is Lossless or Max. - 💽 A track already on disk that Waves has no record of (after a reset, or written by another computer) is recorded when a download finds it, so its button settles instead of reading DOWNLOAD forever. - 🔢 A complete album with music videos no longer shows as partly in your library. - ⚙️ A settings file that cannot be written no longer stops Waves from starting during its one-time video setting migration. - 🗂️ Signing out or resetting while a page snapshot was being saved no longer leaves the old account's pages on disk. - 🪟 On Windows, a preferences write that collides with an antivirus scan is retried instead of dropped. - 🧵 A network folder that stops answering no longer piles up one stuck check after another for as long as it is down. - 🔗 Editorial page links from TIDAL are fetched only when they point inside TIDAL's own API. - 🧹 The artist credits kept for shown rows are cleared at sign-out, a queue row that is cleared frees its progress state, and decorative animations stop while the window is hidden. - 🪟 On Windows, clicking Restart hours after an update was installed now applies the update instead of just closing Waves. - 🪟 On Windows, an update that could not be applied because the install folder was in use now says so instead of asking for a restart again and again. - 🍺 A Homebrew-managed update shows Downloading, Installing and Finishing instead of Homebrew's own output. - 🛑 Update and FFmpeg install failures show a plain reason instead of raw error text, without folder paths or other machine details. - 🪟 On Windows, updating or removing the managed FFmpeg works while a download or preview is still using it. - 💾 An update copy that runs out of disk space no longer leaves a partial copy next to the app. - 🔏 A release without a signed checksum manifest is refused before the download starts, and a pre-release build is offered its final release. - 📜 My Tidal tabs now open at the very top instead of a few pixels down, so the first row no longer sits tight under the tab bar.

body:
🌊 If you enjoy Waves, a star on this repo goes a long way, and if you'd like to help me afford to keep developing it, consider donating.

### 🐛 Fixed - 🎚️ A track you already hold at the best quality TIDAL offers for it no longer keeps offering DOWNLOAD TRACK under a Max setting, where a click fetched nothing: the button now judges the copy the way the download does, so a mixed-quality playlist reads as downloaded once it is ([issue #40](https://github.com/iamprivacy/Waves/issues/40)).

name: v0.1.29
body:
🌊 If you enjoy Waves, a star on this repo goes a long way, and if you'd like to help me afford to keep developing it, consider donating.

### ✨ Added - 🆕 Albums and tracks released in the last two weeks carry a small NEW mark, which stops pulsing once you have them, including on each track of an album page. ### 🔧 Changed - 📁 Waves only counts copies you already have in your download or library folder. ### 🐛 Fixed - 📚 A copy you already have reads DOWNLOADED or IN LIBRARY, and its button names the folder it is in ([issue #38](https://github.com/iamprivacy/Waves/issues/38)). - 🔍 Pasted searches find results again, and an empty or failed search says so ([issue #39](https://github.com/iamprivacy/Waves/issues/39)). - 📅 Album pages show the full release date at the top, not just the year. - 🖼️ Cover art you have already seen appears at once instead of loading again. - ❌ A queued discography or playlist reads QUEUED until it starts, and its ✕ cancels the whole batch. - 🔔 Queue section headings bounce the count that went up, not the one that fell. - 🧾 A single in the download queue no longer offers to expand. - 🖱️ Moving the pointer down the queue no longer makes cards twitch. - 📅 Reissues and anniversary editions show and sort by their own release date. - 🌊 The launch wave animation stays smooth while the library is checked.

name: v0.1.28
body:
🌊 If you enjoy Waves, a star on this repo goes a long way, and if you'd like to help me afford to keep developing it, consider donating.

### ✨ Added - 🎼 A new Settings switch, "Show every edition on artist pages", lists every edition again when "Most-complete edition only" is on and the page would otherwise hide some. ### 🔧 Changed - 🎼 With "Most-complete edition only" on, an artist page no longer lists an edition whose songs are all inside a fuller edition of the same album, so the page shows what a discography download would actually fetch. - ⚡ Album covers you have already loaded are kept, so a page you come back to draws its artwork straight away instead of fetching it again. - ⚡ Resting the pointer on an artist card starts loading that artist, so the page is usually ready by the time you click it. - ⚡ A search Waves can already answer from what it is holding paints at once and corrects itself when the full results arrive, instead of showing nothing until they do. ### 🐛 Fixed - 📚 A large music library kept on a network share is read correctly on macOS. Some shares hand back only part of the folder list, which left albums you already had looking missing, so they could be downloaded a second time. Waves now spots a short listing, finds the missing folders by name, and reads the share again over a fresh connection. - 🎬 The video results grid no longer leaves a gap in its last row. - ⚙️ If your settings file is ever damaged (a power cut or a crash mid-save), Waves keeps a copy of it beside the original and starts on the defaults, instead of quietly saving the defaults over your only copy. - 📚 On a share that treats two spellings of a name as two folders, both artists stay in your library instead of one being dropped as a duplicate. - 📚 An album downloaded by a version before 0.1.17 into a folder with a replaced character is recognised as already yours again, so it is not fetched a second time. - 🎛️ The two controls on a browse console card no longer draw through each other.

name: v0.1.27
body:
🌊 If you enjoy Waves, a star on this repo goes a long way, and if you'd like to help me afford to keep developing it, consider donating.

### ✨ Added - 🎚️ Download one album or song in a different quality without touching Settings: click its quality badge and pick a tier from the menu. The badge keeps showing your choice, and downloads of that item keep asking for it, until you pick another tier or close Waves; a choice made on an album applies to every song in it ([issue #36](https://github.com/iamprivacy/Waves/issues/36)). - 📚 The quality menu marks the tier you already have on disk, so a song or album is not downloaded again in a quality you are holding ([issue #36](https://github.com/iamprivacy/Waves/issues/36)). - ✖️ The download queue has its own close button, so you no longer have to click the page behind it to put the panel away. ### 🔧 Changed - ↩️ Collapsing an expanded album or playlist row folds it shut as the page scrolls back to where it was before you opened it, instead of snapping shut and leaving you further down the page. ### 🐛 Fixed - ⬇️ The small download button on a song row is dark green again, like every other button, instead of a white tile.

name: v0.1.26
body:
🌊 If you enjoy Waves, a star on this repo goes a long way, and if you'd like to help me afford to keep developing it, consider donating.

### 🔧 Changed - 🏷️ Waves' internal code now carries its own name instead of the name of the project it began as a fork of; nothing changes in how the app looks or works, and the credits to that project remain. - 🐢 The two rate-limit settings in Advanced now do what they say: Waves pauses for the set number of seconds after every N songs, so a long playlist does not ask TIDAL for too much at once. They are now called "Pause every N songs" and "Length of that pause (s)", and setting either to 0 turns the pause off ([issue #35](https://github.com/iamprivacy/Waves/issues/35)). - ⏱️ A pause length over 30 seconds goes back to its standard value on this update; everything else is left exactly as you set it. Check both settings after updating: a "3" that used to mean three albums now means a pause every three songs. - 🔒 On macOS and Linux, the files Waves keeps for itself (your settings, your sign-in and its caches) are now created readable by your account only, rather than by anyone else with an account on the same machine. Existing files take the new permissions the next time Waves saves them. - 🆔 Downloaded songs now carry the TIDAL id of every artist they are credited to; players and library tools skip fields they do not know, so nothing looks or sounds different. It can only describe songs downloaded from this version onward. - 📦 The app is a smaller download and takes up less space once installed. - 🖼️ Downloading an album fetches its cover art once instead of once per track, so albums finish a little faster. - ⚡ Scanning a large library keeps the app responsive while the scan runs. - 🧠 Long download sessions use less memory. - 🚀 Launch is a little quicker. - 🔎 Search results appear sooner. ### 🐛 Fixed - 🔎 Search now keeps up to 60 matching artists instead of 12, so a lesser-known artist who shares a name with a famous one can actually be found by expanding the ARTISTS row. - 🎛️ The Artists/Albums/Tracks filter above search results no longer carries over to the next search: every search starts back on All, so a filter picked earlier can no longer hide the artist you just searched for. - 👻 Opening Search no longer shows a lone "SHOW LESS" on an empty page, before any search has been run. - 🌊 The wave animation on the launch screen plays noticeably smoother while the app loads. - 🎤 An artist's page no longer lists a top song that belongs to a different artist with the same name, and holding the pointer on an artist to preview no longer plays one. - 💿 Downloading a discography no longer saves albums by a different artist with the same name: a release TIDAL wrongly files under the chosen artist is skipped and counted in the log. - 🔢 A song from an album TIDAL will not describe in full is no longer tagged "track 7 of 1": the total is left out when it is not known, so players and library tools stop reading the album as complete at one song. - 📄 With "Create .m3u8 playlist" on, re-downloading an album you already have no longer replaces a playlist file the folder already held: Waves now writes a playlist only in folders it actually saved a song into, so a playlist you made yourself (or one from before you used Waves) is left alone. - 🏷️ Songs saved as .m4a no longer carry blank extra fields (lyrics, UPC, initial key, release type) that tag editors showed as empty rows; the same song saved as FLAC never had them. - 💨 Expanding an album in search results no longer pauses for a moment the first time, on the way to showing its songs. - 🕵️ An exported diagnostics report with "also hide titles and searches" checked no longer shows the names of songs, albums and folders in its move, skip and error lines; they are hidden like every other title. - 📋 Pasting the wrong thing into the sign-in box (say, a stray clipboard entry) is now refused with a hint instead of being written into the app's log. - 🎤 An artist page that fails to load no longer leaves that artist unclickable until the next sign-in, and no longer leaves the loading spinner turning; the same slip could freeze a search or a pasted link on its "Searching" message. - 🚪 Signing out now discards any search still in flight, so its results can no longer flash up over "Signed out" or be shown to the next account that signs in. - 👥 Running two copies of Waves at once can no longer scramble the remembered window layout and interface state, and can no longer trip up an FFmpeg install the other copy is doing at the same time. - 📅 A song saved by an older version into an album folder named "[None]" (an album TIDAL lists no release year for) no longer blocks downloading it again: fetching the album again now saves it under the corrected folder name, though the old "[None]" copy stays for you to remove. - 🔢 The artist badge in Library no longer reports a track count higher than any copy on disk when two differently structured editions of the same album are both present. - 💿 A song TIDAL served at a lower quality than it advertises no longer reads as fully downloaded for good: it counts as one to fetch again, so raising the quality setting or re-running the album picks it up. If TIDAL keeps handing back the same lower quality, Waves stops asking after two tries and keeps what it has, so an album cannot re-download itself every time you open it; Redownload asks again. - 🔂 A playlist that lists the same song twice now saves it once, instead of leaving a second identical copy numbered "\_01" beside it that nothing would ever clean up or notice again, and the second listing is reported as skipped rather than as a failed song, which could finish a whole playlist in red over a song sitting correctly on disk. - 🎬 A mix no longer downloads its music videos when music videos are switched off; every other kind of list already left them alone. - 📃 An empty playlist, or one holding only videos, now finishes quietly instead of reporting "Failed: no tracks were downloaded" over a list that had nothing in it. - 🔤 On drives that store accented names their own way (many external Mac disks and network shares), a playlist file again lists its songs in the playlist's order rather than the order they happened to finish in. - 🪟 On Windows, saving to a mapped network drive with "link to the track" turned on no longer fails the whole playlist at its last step with every song already saved. - 🛟 A song that has already landed in your library is no longer sometimes reported as failed anyway, which also cost it its lyrics and cover. - 📝 A settings file that has been corrupted into something Waves cannot read is moved aside and replaced, as intended, instead of stopping the app from starting at all. - 🔑 Pasting your sign-in link back no longer leaves the spinner turning over an app that still says signed out; that could happen even though the sign-in had gone through, and restarting picked it up. - 🧹 A factory reset now removes everything the updater and the FFmpeg installer leave behind, including the note of a downloaded update waiting to be applied, which recorded the folder Waves is installed in; before, any one of those leftovers kept the whole folder, and the folders it named, on disk. - 🈶 A very long song title in Chinese, Japanese, Korean or similar is now shortened by only as much as the path really needs, instead of losing half its name. - 📁 On Windows, a song saved into a very deeply nested folder no longer fails every attempt. - ⚙️ A section closing in Settings no longer blanks its contents before the section itself has finished closing. - 🔁 On Windows, an update you installed but have not restarted into yet is picked up again the next time you open Waves, so leaving the app open all day (or shutting the PC down instead of restarting) no longer leaves you quietly on the old version. - 🪟 Having two copies of Waves open at once can no longer spoil an update: one of them installs it and the other is told to restart, instead of both writing over the same half-finished files. - 🔤 On Windows, an update now applies whatever the folder it lives under is called: letters outside the English alphabet, an "&", a percent sign; before, Waves said it had updated and then quietly stayed on the old version, every time. - ⚡ On Windows, an update now finishes in an instant when you quit Waves, instead of copying the new version into place while the PC is shutting down, which could leave the app broken until you repaired the folder by hand. - 📁 Installing an update no longer deletes files you kept in the Waves folder: anything in there that Waves did not put there is moved back after the update, and if something cannot be moved back the old folder is kept instead of deleted. When that happens Waves now names the folder it kept, so you can delete it yourself once you no longer need it, instead of it sitting there unmentioned, and later updates leave that folder alone rather than clearing it to make room for their own backup. - 📃 A long playlist no longer fails over a song TIDAL has taken down: one song it no longer carries used to fail the whole playlist, every time you tried, so a 200 or 500 song playlist could never finish ([issue #35](https://github.com/iamprivacy/Waves/issues/35)). - ⚠️ A failed album, playlist or mix now says how many songs failed, and out of how many, instead of only "Failed", so you can tell a download that saved almost everything from one that saved nothing ([issue #35](https://github.com/iamprivacy/Waves/issues/35)). - 🔁 A busy download no longer gives up on a song the first time TIDAL asks it to slow down: Waves waits and tries again, which is what long playlists kept running into ([issue #35](https://github.com/iamprivacy/Waves/issues/35)). - 🧯 One song that goes wrong mid-download no longer stops the rest of the playlist: the other songs finish, the playlist file is still written, and the queue reports how many were missed ([issue #35](https://github.com/iamprivacy/Waves/issues/35)). - 🏷️ A playlist song whose album details are missing now downloads and is tagged with what is known, instead of failing. - 🗂️ An album TIDAL lists no release year for now lands in a folder named after the album alone, instead of one beginning with "[None]". - 📻 A download that stops answering can no longer hold the queue up forever waiting on it. - 🛑 Pressing STOP while Waves is checking that your download folder is reachable now sticks: the row could go back to Downloading and the button re-light, until the whole list had been read. - ♻️ A REDOWNLOAD you cancelled or cleared before it started no longer forces the next download of that item: a later click on it, from a discography or a folder, could re-download and overwrite songs you already had without asking. - 🔁 RETRY ALL no longer loses the rows behind one that cannot be restarted: the others retry, and the one that could not keeps its place with its RETRY button. - 🎨 An artist download whose albums are waiting for a folder that went away now keeps its progress: the artist button went back to plain DOWNLOAD and never reported the albums that downloaded when the folder came back. - 🎯 An artist or folder download that finishes with every album saved no longer ends on FAILED because one of them failed on an earlier attempt in the same run. - 💿 Stopping a discography download no longer makes the next Download album on one of its albums skip the check for a more complete edition ("best of both"). - 🔀 Returning to the Search tab now brings back the whole artist page you left: it could come back as one artist's name and photo over another artist's albums and songs, with the download button aimed at the wrong one. - 📋 Opening a queued or failed album, playlist or mix to see its songs now works after a new search, instead of showing an empty list. - 🎧 Saving an audio quality change while a Dolby Atmos song is being fetched no longer lands on that song: it could be downloaded at the wrong quality, or fail to download at all, with nothing to connect it to the setting you had just saved. - 🔊 A Dolby Atmos song you already have is never replaced by a stereo download of it, or the other way round: TIDAL hands both out under the same file name, so with "Skip existing" turned off, on a REDOWNLOAD, or after a quality change, the new one could land on top of the one you kept. Each is now saved beside the other, and an Atmos file you added yourself is protected the same way. - 💬 The message shown when something you download is already in your music library now says what will actually happen under your "Skip existing" setting, instead of always promising that your existing files are never touched. - 🧷 Having two copies of Waves open no longer risks your settings or your sign-in: they could write over each other's saved file, which reset everything to factory defaults or signed you out on the next launch. - 🚀 Opening Waves twice on the first run after an update no longer stops the second one from starting. - 🎬 Double-clicking INSTALL FFMPEG now installs it once, instead of downloading it twice at the same time and then saying "Install failed" over an install that worked. - 🔢 The download queue header says "1 item" rather than "1 items". - 🎚️ An album already at the best quality its release offers no longer keeps showing DOWNLOAD after you raise the audio quality setting, where clicking it finished at once and changed nothing. - 📁 A discography no longer ends on FAILED when your download folder went to sleep between albums: the albums that waited for it are counted when they arrive, not the moment they are held. - 📂 Choosing a new download location while albums are waiting for the old one no longer leaves that artist's button turning for the rest of the session, with an empty queue and no STOP to end it. - 🧹 Clearing the queue no longer leaves an album downloading with no row to show it and no STOP on screen: a download that had only just started is now stopped along with its row. - 🛑 STOP, CANCEL and clearing the queue now all end downloads that were waiting for your download folder to come back, instead of them starting again by themselves minutes later once it did, with no row on screen to stop them a second time. - 🎛️ Turning "best of both" off now applies to an album whose earlier merged download you cleared, stopped, or left waiting for a folder you then changed: clicking it again saves the edition you chose, instead of quietly combining two. - 🎨 Clearing the queue no longer counts an album that had just begun downloading as failed, which could leave the artist or folder it belonged to reporting a failure that never happened.

name: v0.1.24
body:
🌊 If you enjoy Waves, a star on this repo goes a long way, and if you'd like to help me afford to keep developing it, consider donating.

### ✨ Added - 💿 Playlist pages have a "Download full albums" button that saves the complete album each song comes from, one copy per album ([issue #4](https://github.com/iamprivacy/Waves/issues/4)). - 🎯 Search for a specific song, album, video or playlist and it appears as a Top result above everything else on the All page, so the thing you typed is the first row rather than the first row under the artists. - 📈 Search results can be sorted by Popularity again, alongside Relevance, Release date and Name. - 🔁 The search sort you pick (and its direction) is remembered, so Waves opens on it next time. ### 🔧 Changed - ⏹️ STOP keeps what it stopped: every queued or running download stays in the queue, in a new Stopped section you can retry or clear. It used to empty the queue ([issue #27](https://github.com/iamprivacy/Waves/issues/27)). - ⚙️ On "Download discography", "Best of both" and the other edition choices now follow "Most-complete edition only": with that switched off, every edition of an album is saved as it is. Saving a single album with "Best of both" is unchanged ([issue #27](https://github.com/iamprivacy/Waves/issues/27)). - 🖼️ Open a playlist, album or mix from its card and its cover and title are on screen at once, while the songs are still on their way. They used to appear only once the whole page was ready. - ⚡ Rest the pointer on a playlist, album or mix card for a moment and the click that follows opens the page at once, covers included. Resting on a song does the same for the album it comes from. - 🖼️ An artist's page shows their picture straight away when you open it from a card that already shows it. - ⚡ Rest the pointer on an album row for a moment and the click that expands it shows its songs at once, instead of the list popping in after the panel has opened. - 🖼️ The round cover on a song row shows a loading mark until it arrives, and says so when a song has no cover at all. It used to be a blank grey circle in both cases. - 💾 Waves keeps four times as many covers on your computer, so pages you have opened before come back faster. - ⏳ While a page loads, a light travels along a row of cells under the "Reading the wire…" line. ### 🐛 Fixed - 🐢 The window no longer gets slower and slower as a long download session piles up waiting, failed and stopped rows: with thousands of items in the queue it stays as quick as with ten, so a session that runs day and night does not need a restart to feel right again ([issue #30](https://github.com/iamprivacy/Waves/issues/30)). - ⏳ RETRY ALL and STOP over thousands of rows act at once instead of freezing the window, and downloads waiting in the queue take almost no memory until their turn comes, so you can queue tens of thousands of songs and albums ([issue #30](https://github.com/iamprivacy/Waves/issues/30)). - 🔁 RETRY on a failed or stopped download always works straight away, even after later searches: the queue keeps what it needs to try again, instead of asking TIDAL for the album all over again first. - ⏹️ STOP now ends a discography, videos or editions download that has not reached the queue yet, and stays on screen while Waves works out what to download. Those songs used to arrive in the queue after the press, with no STOP left to press ([issue #27](https://github.com/iamprivacy/Waves/issues/27)). - 🎬 Pages full of videos (search results, an artist's videos, your saved videos) fill in faster and use much less data. - 📋 The Paste button in the search bar searches short terms too. Pasting three characters or fewer put the text in the box and then did nothing at all ([issue #28](https://github.com/iamprivacy/Waves/issues/28)). - 📁 An album whose title is nothing but a dot gets a folder of its own, named ．. Its songs used to be saved loose in the artist's folder, mixed in with every other album that landed there. Songs you already saved the old way stay where they are ([issue #29](https://github.com/iamprivacy/Waves/issues/29)). - 🔑 A Dolby Atmos song can no longer cost you your sign-in. If TIDAL turned the Atmos request away mid-download, Waves quietly dropped your saved sign-in and you had to sign in again the next time you opened it ([issue #30](https://github.com/iamprivacy/Waves/issues/30)). - 🧹 "Reset Waves completely" now removes the saved cover pictures too. - ⏹️ Signing out stops the downloads first, leaving them in the queue's Stopped section. They used to carry on against the account you had just left, failing one by one ([issue #30](https://github.com/iamprivacy/Waves/issues/30)). - 🪟 Updating Waves on Windows can no longer leave the Waves folder empty: if the update does not arrive whole, the version you already have is kept and started instead. An update you put off restarting for is still applied whenever you do restart. - 🧑‍🎤 A search's Artists view keeps its cards at their normal size when only one or two artists match. They used to stretch to fill the window, so tall that their buttons sat below the fold. - 🔎 Sorting search results by Relevance keeps TIDAL's order, so a song or album you searched for by name and artist comes first even if it came out this week. Relevance used to order by popularity, which put a brand-new single under older songs that shared a word with your search.
